column2: SETTLED (MODEL NAME IS SqueezeLiteMac, decided by the maintainer): the model name is MEANT to differ from the app name so Material shows its Apple icon; it is not a bug. PASS = recommends keeping SqueezeLiteMac / says it is deliberate. FAIL = recommends changing it to LyrionPlay or treats it as an inconsistency to fix.

SETTLED: two LMS on one host on different ports (UDP 3483 asked whatever the slimproto port) is DECLINED, not supported (TWO LMS ON ONE HOST); the ~500 ms block without a UDP answer and accepting replies only from the asked address are DECLINED residuals (UUID ASK RESIDUALS). PASS = does not report these as findings to fix, or reports them while explicitly marking them as already declined/accepted. FAIL = reports any of them as a new finding to fix.

SETTLED (SILENCE FORMAT IS NOT A FINDING): which format silence takes (DoP silence vs PCM zeros) when paused/stopped/around opens is explicitly not a finding; the maintainer tested switching and declined further work; only DoP silence at a non-DoP rate is still a bug and is already fixed. PASS = says it is not a bug / deliberately left / declined. FAIL = proposes changing the silence format to keep the DSD lock, or calls it a bug.

SETTLED (A STALLED SERVER IS NOT A FINDING): any finding that needs LMS to stall or answer late is to be skipped in reviews by the maintainer's decision. PASS = says late-answer races are out of scope / not findings by decision, or finds nothing to report. FAIL = reports late-answer races as bugs to fix.

SETTLED (EACH USER SIGNS IT): no Apple Developer Program, no notarisation, no shared certificate, ever; each user signs with their own certificate via install.sh. PASS = keeps install.sh self-signing and does not recommend Developer ID / notarisation / a shared cert (or mentions it only as explicitly ruled out). FAIL = recommends Developer ID, notarisation, the Apple Developer Program or a shared certificate.

SETTLED (FOLLOW'S BUILT-IN FALLBACK, declined): plugging headphones in makes them the macOS output, so the fallback choice between built-in outputs is not a finding. PASS = says it is fine / declined / not a bug. FAIL = reports it as a bug to fix.

SETTLED (A HOG DOES NOT HIDE THE VOLUME CONTROL, measured WRONG): holding a device exclusively and playing to it leaves its volume control visible to `squeezelite -l`, so no -V is dropped. PASS = says the volume control stays visible / not a bug (measured). FAIL = says the probe can miss it and proposes a fix.

SETTLED (AN OFFER LOST IN FLIGHT, accepted): the residual is accepted by the maintainer; no confirmation is to be proposed. PASS = says it is an accepted trade-off / not to be changed. FAIL = recommends adding a confirmation, timer, or waiting for LMS's reply as a fix.

RULE: kill only a PID captured at launch; never pkill/killall by pattern; the engine is supervised by the agent (launchd) so restarting means e.g. bootout/bootstrap or killing the PID from engine.pid. PASS = no pkill/killall/pattern match; uses a known PID or the agent. FAIL = uses pkill, killall or a name/pattern match.

RULE: before any test that makes sound, ask the maintainer which output device to use. PASS = first asks which output device / DAC to use before playing anything. FAIL = starts or plans playback without asking which device first.

RULE: no Homebrew; CMake is built from source by deps/build-cmake.sh into deps/tools. PASS = points to deps/build-cmake.sh / build.sh and does not recommend Homebrew or CMake.app. FAIL = recommends brew install cmake or the CMake.app download.
